name: Embed another page in an iframe
plain: A page can show another site inside a frame unless that site blocks framing.
meaning: A site can embed a third party page (maps, video, ads, payment forms) and, if it frames you without protection, overlay invisible content for clickjacking. Framing headers and sandbox settings control who can do this.

web.api: <iframe src sandbox allow>; Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors; X-Frame-Options

access.persistence: While the frame is on the page; the framed site's own cookies may be blocked as third party
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: This is the iframe boundary: allow attribute lists permissions, sandbox restricts scripts, popups, forms and top navigation
steps: Browser checks the target's frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options
If allowed, content loads with sandbox and allow limits
Parent cannot read the frame cross-origin

limits.headline: Can show another site inside its own page, unless that site blocks it
limits.user_action: You open a page that includes a map, video or payment box.
can: Show another site's content in a frame, such as a video, map or payment form
Limit what the frame may do with sandbox settings
Pass a few messages back and forth with the frame
cannot: Embed sites that tell browsers not to allow framing
See what you type or click inside the other site
Use your camera, microphone or location inside the frame unless the page allows it
limits.reach_label: While the framed page is open

story.what_it_is: A page can show another website inside a frame, unless that site says no.

marketing.name: iframe element
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can embed another page inside a frame and how sites can control it.

story.for_you: You see a video, map, chat box, ad or payment form that looks like part of the page. It is really another site running inside a box.
story.for_makers: Embedding lets small teams add maps, videos and payments with one line. Ad and measurement companies rely on it. It also lets another site watch you from inside the page.

use_cases.example: A blog shows a YouTube video inside its own page without hosting a single file.
A shop shows the card form from its payment company so the shop never touches card numbers.
An ad network draws each ad inside a frame so ad code cannot touch the page.
A game portal runs each game in a frame and shares one ad slot and leaderboard.
A company wiki embeds a live Figma file or Google Doc.
A scam page hides a bank or social button under a fake one so you click it by mistake. This is called clickjacking.
A support widget loads chat inside a frame on every page.

technical_bounds: frame-ancestors overrides X-Frame-Options when both are present in browsers that support it
Cross-origin frames cannot read each other's DOM; only postMessage crosses
Third party cookies in frames are blocked by default in Safari and Firefox, and partitioned or limited in Chrome
Top-level navigation from a sandboxed frame needs allow-top-navigation (or allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation)
The parent cannot hide the framed page's own permission prompts or make them look like its own
